PullRequest.Title: sessions: Restructure filters and preserve creation provenance
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Restructure the Agents Window's **Filter Sessions** menu so users can distinguish where a session runs, which harness it uses, and which application created it.

- Add independent **Environment**, **Created In**, and **Harness** filters. Remote environments use stable identifiers rather than editable display names; only connected hosts appear as environment choices.
- Persist creating-application provenance through agent-host creation, discovery, catalog projection, caching, and restore. Cloud sessions use `event_type`, and adoption preserves the creating application. The agent-host metadata is an optional namespaced extension; existing hosts and legacy cloud ownership records remain supported.
- Put **Ordering**, **Grouping**, **Show**, **External**, and the metadata filters directly in the menu, with current values in single-choice submenu titles. **Show Done** is a direct toggle.
- Scope **Created In** to included environments without clearing saved application selections. Keep Local, Cloud, and remote-host groups separated, without group headings. Preserve cached sources for included disconnected hosts, summarize restricted environment selections, and explain empty application menus. Cloud Slack and Teams applications are excluded by default.
- Remove status, Read, and Empty Groups filters; keep empty user-created groups visible and retain Sort and Find on mobile. **Compact View** and **Collapse All Groups** stay in the Filter Sessions menu.

Includes regression tests, accessibility help, and session architecture documentation.

The final Created In rename and environment-scoping refinement are covered by unit tests, not by those earlier screenshots. Live cloud/remote-backend integration was not exercised.

## How to Test

1. Open the Agents Window and **Filter Sessions**. Change Ordering and Grouping and verify their titles reflect the selection. With Workspace grouping, switch Show between Recent and All.
2. Exclude Cloud under Environment. Verify cloud applications disappear from Created In and the Environment title summarizes the selection. Include Cloud again and verify saved application choices return.
3. Verify harness, application, and Done selections do not prune the application catalog or change environment selections. Exclude every environment to see **Select an Environment First**; an included environment with no known applications should instead show **No Applications Found**.
4. With suitable sessions, verify Slack/Teams cloud defaults, per-environment application choices, and persistence after reload. Rename or disconnect a remote host and verify its saved selections remain associated with its stable identity.
5. Check keyboard submenu navigation, Show Done, Compact View, Collapse All Groups, and Reset Filters. On phone layout, confirm Sort and Find remain available.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path, per-task placement, full-map reconstruction, 1,000-record bound, and optional event_type fallback are all explicit in changed code and tests. Exact task counts vary, affecting severity but not the repeated-work mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and temporary Map/object allocations while decoding persisted ownership records
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For M visible tasks whose API response omits event_type and H persisted ownership records, this performs O(M×H) record validation and Map insertion; H is explicitly allowed to grow to 1,000.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased cloud-session list refresh latency plus extension-host CPU and GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: fetchSessionList read ownership once through getOwnedTaskIds(), built one Set, and reused its isExternal closure for every returned task, so ownership decoding was O(H) per refresh.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each no-event_type task now calls CloudTaskOwnership.getApplication(), which invokes _read(), enumerates the entire stored ownership object, validates every record, and rebuilds a Map before looking up one task ID.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 1484 inserts this._ownership.getApplication(entry.taskId) into the per-session map; before the PR the metadata expression only used the already-snapshotted isExternal lookup.
Findings.Title: Reuse the ownership snapshot across the session-list map
Findings.Impact: Opening or periodically refreshing a cloud-session list containing legacy/tasks-without-event_type repeatedly rebuilds the up-to-1,000-entry ownership map once per such task, delaying publication of the refreshed list and creating avoidable garbage on the extension host.
Findings.Evidence: provideChatSessionItems maps all sessionList entries at lines 1457+, and line 1484 performs getApplication(entry.taskId) inside that map. CloudTaskOwnership.getApplication calls _read().get; _read iterates Object.entries(stored) into a new Map, while MAX_OWNED_CLOUD_TASKS is 1000. The same refresh already reads ownership once at fetchSessionList line 1413, proving a reusable per-refresh snapshot exists conceptually. eventType is optional and the added TaskApiBackend test explicitly covers undefined, so the fallback path is real.
Findings.Recommendation: Read ownership once per provideChatSessionItems refresh and reuse that snapshot for both external status and application lookup (for example return a taskId→record snapshot/lookup closure from fetchSessionList), rather than calling _read() from each mapped task.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold or expired Copilot cloud-session list refresh, including legacy tasks whose Task API response omits event_type
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository resolution and the Task API session-list request must complete, then all visible session-item promises (including existing PR/diff enrichment) and the new provenance metadata construction must finish before session items are published. The reported ownership decoding runs synchronously inside each mapped item and is therefore on this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch cloud task/session summaries from the Task API
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list request per cold/expired/coalesced refresh; repository grouping and session filtering happen around that request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Task API list request occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before item construction and publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve pull artifacts and changed files for visible sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per visible task with the relevant PR/diff metadata, run through the existing Promise.all item fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-visible-session enrichment occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All item promises must settle before the refreshed list is published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate and validate persisted ownership records into a new Map
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per visible task lacking event_type, each time over all H ownership records; effective cost O(M×H).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ownership was decoded once per refresh by getOwnedTaskIds and reused through isExternal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation work delays completion of each item and therefore the whole refreshed list.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M visible tasks without event_type after external-session filtering, multiplied by H persisted ownership records; H is bounded at 1,000. Tasks with event_type short-circuit the new lookup, so effective multiplicity is only the no-event_type subset.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent callers are coalesced by chatSessionItemsPromise, and a warm cachedSessionItems value bypasses item reconstruction. Item enrichment uses existing Promise.all concurrency; the ownership-map rebuilds are synchronous and occur once in each affected item callback, with no shared snapshot.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm cachedSessionItems avoids the regression until expiry or explicit refresh. On a cold/expired refresh, fetchSessionList snapshots owned task IDs once, but getApplication independently rereads and reconstructs ownership state for each missing-event_type task. Ownership history is bounded to 1,000 records; there is no per-refresh application snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed per-item call, full-map reconstruction, optional event_type fallback, cache path, and 1,000-record bound are explicit in code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The proportion of real Task API responses without event_type and typical ownership-history size vary; this uncertainty lowers severity but does not affect the quadratic mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated-work regression; submitted through report_finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sessions view initialization, provider/session updates, filter changes, and opening the Filter Sessions menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view's reactive menu state synchronously reads providers and sessions, builds environment/application options, and updates global menu/action registrations when the structurally compared option state changes. List filtering also synchronously checks three filter keys per session before rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: N known sessions, E distinct environments/providers, and A distinct environment/application options. getSessionFilterOptions scans sessions once per ordered environment (O(E×N)); E is normally local/cloud plus connected remote hosts, while registrations scale with A rather than all sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is synchronous on the UI thread. Event.any does not debounce updates, but derivedOpts with structuralEquals prevents downstream action re-registration when a generic session-change event leaves filter options unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Filter preferences are loaded once from profile storage and retained in a Map. Provider session catalogs and application observables supply in-memory data; no cold network/filesystem read occurs in menu computation. Disconnected remote providers are excluded as choices while cached session applications can remain represented.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous O(E×N) scan and structural-equality suppression; both are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large session catalogs and many simultaneous remote hosts could increase UI-thread cost, but realistic E is small and the diff does not prove sufficiently frequent or costly updates beyond existing list-wide refresh work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the computation is collection-wide but bounded by normally small environment cardinality, and unchanged option states suppress costly registration churn.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a local or remote agent-host session and persist creating-application provenance
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider session creation completes, then non-ephemeral sessions await a per-session SQLite metadata write for the initiator before registry registration and createSession completion. Registry registration was already awaited afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the per-session SQLite database and atomically write SESSION_INITIATOR_METADATA_KEY
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transaction for every newly created non-ephemeral session; before the diff only sessions with creation-reference, dev-container-worktree, or remote-origin metadata entered this persistence block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary sessions without the three special metadata kinds skipped this per-session metadata transaction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before registry registration and before createSession returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register the created session in the session registry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registry mutation per non-ephemeral creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same registry mutation followed provider creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One protocol request per session creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create-session IPC existed; the diff only adds initiator metadata to its payload/config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The client waits for the server-side creation and persistence path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initiator record per newly created non-ephemeral session; cost is constant per user creation and does not fan out over existing sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider creation and side-effect initialization remain parallelized as before. The new SQLite metadata transaction is serialized on the individual createSession critical path before the existing registry mutation; no new aggregate concurrency burst is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache bypasses the initial persistence. Subsequent list/restore reads include the initiator in existing batched metadata reads, and browser-side startup cache serialization is capped at 100 sessions per host.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that one extra SQLite write is added to ordinary non-ephemeral creation and is awaited.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No repository evidence shows this single small transaction causing material creation latency relative to provider setup and registry I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this is a constant, required durability write per explicit creation, without demonstrated material impact or multiplicative scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cloud sandbox discovery and agent-host catalog projection/restore
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing task-list/full-task network discovery resolves sandbox bindings; the diff copies event_type from those existing responses into discovered-session metadata. Restore/list paths read the initiator as one additional key in existing bulk metadata queries and project it through caches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch task details used for sandbox discovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing task-list/full-task discovery cardinality; event_type is read from already-fetched summary/full objects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same task discovery network requests occurred without retaining event_type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing discovery waits for these calls; the diff adds no request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bulk-read persisted session metadata during restore/catalog resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing bulk query per restored/resolved session, now requesting one additional key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bulk query read the other metadata keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already on restore/catalog critical paths; no separate query is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize initiator/provider scalars in per-host cached session metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cached adapter when cache persistence runs, capped at 100 retained entries per host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cached entries omitted these small scalar/object fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local storage serialization remains on the existing cache-save path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One metadata field per discovered/restored session. Catalog/startup cache serialization remains capped per host; network request cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing discovery concurrency and caching are unchanged. The added eventType extraction is local constant work within already-running task processing; no new Promise fan-out or limiter bypass appears.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing discovery and inventory caches retain the additional scalar metadata. Cold discovery performs the same network calls; warm inventory/catalog restore reads the additional field from cached data without introducing a separate fetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff only propagates data already returned by existing boundaries and adds batched keys/scalars.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Payload sizes and host counts vary, but the added metadata is small and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: no new network/database fan-out, and added serialization is small and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across the full 81-file inventory. Reported one introduced repeated-work regression in cloud-session item refresh: per-task provenance fallback rebuilds the full persisted ownership map. Reviewed session filter/menu recomputation, agent-host provenance persistence/restore, provider cache serialization, and cloud-sandbox discovery; no other changed mechanism met the evidence and impact threshold.
